The core insight is that team success emerges not from singular star performances but from the statistical distribution of player contributions. The method employs generalized estimating equations (GEE) to model match outcomes as functions of performance indicators, adjusting for interdependence among teams. This allows for quantifying how variability in performance—captured through percentiles like P25 and P50—predicts wins or losses. The derived operators map individual performance into collective outcome space, enabling both retrospective analysis and prospective tactical planning. Dualities arise in interpreting whether reliance on high-performing individuals or balanced distributions yields better results. Failure modes include overfitting due to small sample sizes or ignoring confounding variables such as margin or quarter effects. The framework supports Bayesian updating of player value estimates and provides a foundation for GSE state transitions based on evolving performance kernels.
